# FGSEditor

**FGSEditor** is an open-source graphical tool designed to view, edit, and create Film Grain Synthesis (FGS) tables for AV1 video. It allows you to modify FGS tables generated by [`grav1synth`](https://github.com/rust-av/grav1synth), create new ones from scratch, or generate them using built-in presets.

The editor supports both **static FGS** (single event) and **dynamic FGS** (multiple events).

## 🚀 Features
- Grain value-strength tuning on Luma and Chroma independently
- Dynamic control of value-strength points and interpolated values visualization
- Edit start-end timestamp of individual events with milliseconds precision
- Entire FGS events visualization on an average strength - seconds plot
- Extract video duration and FPS directly from AV1 and HEVC videos
- Robust Autosave system with backups to prevent data loss
- Detailed Settings menu to tune visual colors, timeline fallbacks, and performance constraints
- Mathematical grain strength preview

## 📥 Installation & Usage

### Download Pre-compiled Binaries
You can grab the latest compiled version directly from the Releases page:
1. Go to the [Releases](../../releases) tab.
2. Download the latest binary for your operating system.
3. Extract the archive and run the executable.

> **Note:** FGSEditor requires [`grav1synth`](https://github.com/rust-av/grav1synth) to apply FGS tables directly to video files.
> Download it separately and place `grav1synth` (or `grav1synth.exe` on Windows) next to the FGSEditor executable, or add it to your system `PATH`.

### Build from Source
To build the project locally, simply run the provided `.bat` file (Windows), which uses PyInstaller:
```
build.bat
```

## Fork test build: session persistence and Apply

Video, FGS-table and template-import dialogs remember separate successful-open directories in the existing
`settings.json` next to the application. Missing directories fall back to the application folder.
Main, dynamic timeline and event editor windows independently remember Qt geometry; restoration
checks the available monitors. Minimized state is not persisted.

**Save & Apply** uses the current in-memory table, including unsaved edits. In a dynamic timeline,
it includes the currently open event editor. All event boundaries and gaps are retained; no looping
or extension is added. If no video is associated, select a target AV1 video. Output is always a new
MKV; existing files are protected. grav1synth replaces the grain headers and FFmpeg remuxes with
stream copy, retaining original audio, subtitles, attachments, chapters and metadata where supported.
An unsupported stream fails the operation rather than silently dropping it. Stream order may change
(the edited AV1 video is first). Cancel stops the external process and removes temporary files.
Applying does not mark the table as saved; use Save FGS separately to save the edited table.

The Windows test artifact includes grav1synth. FFmpeg and ffprobe are not bundled;
configure their paths in Settings before video extraction or Save & Apply. BUILD_INFO.txt identifies the source commit and grav1synth release.

Manual checks: restart after moving/resizing each window; test mixed-DPI displays and unplugging
one; cancel/fail file opens; edit extracted grain without saving then Apply; test a dynamic table
with gaps and an open event editor; cancel a long Apply; use Chinese, spaces, apostrophes, ampersands
and parentheses in paths. Compare playback, audio/subtitles, chapters and grain timing with the source.

Texture preview is not implemented in this stage. Future preview can consume the same immutable
`build_dynamic_lines` snapshot used by `apply_current_table`, selecting the event at the preview time.
